title: Radioactivity
description: Some nuclei are unstable and fall apart on their own, at random, but at a rate fixed for each kind. Half of any sample is gone after its half-life, whatever you do to it. Unlocks Radium Salt, the Geiger Tube and Counter, and the Prussian Blue Tablet.

puzzle.goal: Each unstable nucleus has the same small chance λ per second of decaying, whatever the others do. Starting with N _ 0 nuclei, write how many N are left after a time t.
puzzle.name: Radioactive decay law
puzzle.ask: A sample starts with M = @{M} radium nuclei; radium-226 has a half-life T of @{T} years. Find how many remain after t = @{t} years.
puzzle.method: dN/dt = −λN: the decay rate is proportional to what is left. The half-life is the time for exp(−λt) to reach 1/2, so λ = ln 2 / T.
